title: Nobody bought this: price anchoring
voiceStatus: estimated (run a TTS tool with word timestamps and regenerate vo.gen.ts)

vo.text: This $429 bread maker was never meant to sell.
It sat on the shelf. Nobody bought it.
So they added a second one, almost twice the price.
Sales of the cheap one nearly doubled.
Your brain has no idea what a bread maker is worth.
It grabs the first number it sees. That's anchoring.
In 1974, Kahneman and Tversky spun a rigged wheel.
Then asked: what share of UN countries are African?
Wheel said 10: people guessed 25%. Wheel said 65: they guessed 45%.
That's why the menu has a $90 steak, and the tag says was $199.
It's the first number. So ask: who chose it?
